clue.text: Problem brought about by insect around horse

indicators.note: to bring a ship about is to turn it round, so the word for problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is a problem in arithmetic

indicators.note: turned around, so the insect's name runs backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting insect

explanation.surface: A horse is pestered by a biting insect buzzing round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns SUM into MUS and 'around' turns GNAT into TANG; side by side they give the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild horse of the American plains is the example meant.

clue.text: New in post, unknown quantity for the most part

indicators.note: the abbreviation for new is placed inside the word for post

parts.note: post is letters, mail
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: Someone new at the post office is mostly an unknown quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside MAIL to give MAINL, then Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean largely or chiefly, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Composer succeeded with plan, consuming time on last bit of opera

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

indicators.note: the word for plan swallows the letter for time

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word opera is taken

explanation.surface: A composer pulls off a scheme, taking his time over the end of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts T inside MEAN to give METAN; S goes in front and A, the last letter of 'opera', at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was the Czech composer of The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: Pharaoh, mostly correct, with strongly approved record

indicators.note: most of the word for correct is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: to amend a text is to correct it
something hot is very popular, much in favour
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A pharaoh, largely in the right, backed by a much-praised recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from AMEND to leave AMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenhotep was the name of several Egyptian kings of the eighteenth dynasty.

clue.text: Good published song about Cuba, an island

indicators.note: the song is written next to Cuba and an, as a song on that subject would follow its title

parts.note: a newspaper ran a story when it published it
C is the international vehicle registration letter for Cuba
taken as written
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A good song about Cuba was released, describing it as an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Cuba the island; it only supplies C, and the island defined is one of the Canaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran Canaria is one of the Canary Islands, a Spanish group off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Small amount at heart of action removed from account

indicators.note: the small amount sits in the middle of the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
a bit is a small amount

explanation.surface: A small sum taken from the middle of a deal is charged to an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart of' puts BIT in the middle of DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum debited is taken out of, or charged against, a bank balance.

clue.text: Spot date on part of Bible

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, one part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone notices a date written in a section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot and a dot are both small round marks.

clue.text: In 'Bambi' journalist's found word signifying 'small and elegant'

indicators.note: the word sits inside the letters of the clue's next two words

explanation.surface: In the film Bambi, a reporter discovers a word meaning dainty.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'BamBI JOUrnalist's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bijou house or flat is a small, stylish one, from the French for a jewel.

clue.text: Books packed with military intelligence for soldiers

indicators.note: the word for books is filled with the two-letter intelligence abbreviation

parts.note: tomes are large books
MI stands for Military Intelligence, as in MI5

explanation.surface: Books stuffed with army secrets are meant for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: TOMMIES is the old British nickname for ordinary soldiers, from Tommy Atkins.
explanation.definitionFit: British privates were called Tommies, a slang term for rank-and-file troops.

clue.text: Types editor upset, covering celebrity's latest smashes

indicators.note: the reversed letters wrap round the single letter taken from celebrity
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so both words read backwards

parts.note: sorts are types or kinds

indicators.note: the latest letter is the final one of the word

explanation.surface: An editor in a rage over types of fame wrecks things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SORTS + ED into DESTROS; 'covering' wraps that round Y, the last letter of 'celebrity's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash something is to wreck or ruin it, a synonym.

clue.text: Get in lane, having gone wrong — it's awkward

indicators.note: letters that have gone wrong are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A driver muddles the instruction to change lanes, an ungainly move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone wrong' says to rearrange GETINLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy or graceless movement is what both words describe.

clue.text: King with energy in difficult situations

indicators.note: the letter for energy is placed inside the word for tight spots

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in trouble
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A monarch shows vigour when things get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside JAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of England and Scotland bore this name, among them the first Stuart king of England.

clue.text: Learner, with expletive, not keen

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
an oath is a swear word

explanation.surface: A learner driver swears and is reluctant to go on.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant or unwilling is the shared sense.

clue.text: One held responsible for producing theatrical duds?

definitions.text: One held responsible for producing theatrical duds?

parts.words: One held responsible for producing theatrical duds?
parts.note: duds looks like failed shows that someone gets blamed for, but it is slang for clothes, so this is the maker of stage outfits

explanation.surface: Someone is blamed for a string of flops on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duds' suggests theatrical failures; as slang it means clothes, so the person meant supplies stage outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person makes or supplies costumes for plays and films.

clue.text: Son, supported with cries, wins race

indicators.note: in a down clue the son sits on top, held up by what follows

parts.note: to weep is to cry
to take a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A boy, propped up and in tears, still comes first in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported with' puts S above WEEPS in the down entry, then TAKES follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race in which the stakes are pooled and the winner takes all is this kind of event.

clue.text: Insincere talk by a leader of empire (leader of unbelievable cunning) interrupted by king irascibly

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, pious talk

indicators.note: the emperor's name is broken into by the letter for king

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: sly means cunning

explanation.surface: Smooth talk from an emperor, broken off by a king, provokes a bad-tempered reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' puts K inside NERO to give NKERO; 'leader of' takes U from 'unbelievable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting grumpily and quarrelsomely, the adverb of being bad-tempered.

clue.text: Start to speak, detaining one with drink

indicators.note: the word for speak holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone begins to talk while keeping a drinker back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detaining' puts I + GIN inside ORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or arise is to come into being, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Friendly stroll around art gallery

indicators.note: the word for stroll goes round the abbreviation for the gallery

parts.note: to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace
the ICA, the Institute of Contemporary Arts, is a London gallery

explanation.surface: A pleasant wander round an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA is the Institute of Contemporary Arts on the Mall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on good terms, without hostility, is what both words convey.

clue.text: Pocket map, as tripper, I unfolded, going round capital of Oman

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the single letter taken from Oman
a map unfolded is opened out and its letters rearranged
a word's capital is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tourist unfolds a map and pockets it while travelling round Oman's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolded' rearranges MAPASTRIPPERI; 'going round' wraps it round O, the first letter of 'Oman'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket money is to take it for oneself dishonestly, a verb sense.

clue.text: Doctor remains for conference

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor stays on for a medical conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' tells you to rearrange REMAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a meeting for discussion, a type of conference.

clue.text: One not to be trusted with property and gold

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic or property
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone shifty is entrusted with land and bullion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'property' here means a quality, not land.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrayer is someone who cannot be relied upon.

clue.text: Baloney turns up, delivered very hot

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means reads upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense
to deliver someone from something is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: Nonsense surfaces, delivered in sweltering heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' makes ROT read TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorching weather is the sense; a torrid climate is a hot and dry one.

clue.text: Agreeable fellow keeping can't wait until single clues

clue.text: Flowing game with first pair of seeds

parts.note: loo is an old card game

indicators.note: only the opening two letters of the word seeds are taken

explanation.surface: A game played with the first two seeds of a tournament flows freely.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is an old card game; the first two letters of 'seeds' give SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose hair is flowing, hanging free and unbound.

clue.text: State identity-a cry for attention?

parts.note: ID is short for identity
ho is a shout to attract notice

explanation.surface: A form asks for your identity, followed by a shout to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the north-west.

clue.text: Discard, say, in game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
in colloquial speech 'go' means say, as in 'then he goes, no way'

explanation.surface: Throwing away a card, for instance, during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it introduces an example; here it is the colloquial verb go.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game played on cards, called out by a caller.

clue.text: Fake strangely accepted by art gallery initially receiving favour

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are taken into the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a group of British art galleries

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of order, so the letters are rearranged
only the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A forgery is oddly taken in by a gallery that was once well disposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns FAKE into KEAF; 'accepted by' puts it inside TATE (TA-KEAF-TE), then R from 'receiving' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour a parent is to resemble them, a family likeness sense.

clue.text: Absolutely abandoned by ally, drink

indicators.note: the friend's word departs from the longer word for completely

parts.note: totally means absolutely
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Completely deserted by a friend, someone turns to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ALLY out of TOTALLY leaves TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits.

clue.text: Serious attention required by shelter

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
a nest is a snug shelter

explanation.surface: Grave consideration is needed before building a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave in intent.

clue.text: Led to become very angry

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Led to become very angry' (OCR): STEERED is 'Led' plus SEE RED round T, but no clue word signals the insertion of T ('to' would be giving T and placing it at once), so a word seems lost; no search finds the printed clue.
